extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent examiners (Korean jurisdiction / Korean Intellectual Property Office)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on drafting and presenting patent claims under the Korean Patent Act and Enforcement Decree, including composition claims (alloys), claim formalities (independent/dependent claims, numbering, references), deferral of claims, and unity of invention determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alloy composition claims: total composition sum requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim directed to alloy should set forth the invention so that composition range of each component in alloy should be added up to be 100%. Regardless of whether the claim is stated as a close claim (“consisting of”) or an open claim (“comprising”), the total sum of composition range should not be over or under 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the minimum ratio of one component plus the maximum ratios of the others do not reach 100% (or exceed 100%), the claim is unclear and not accepted. Example: Claim listing Cu 40-80%, Zn 10-45%, Sn 1-5%, Be 0.6-3%, Si 0.8-4% — with Cu minimum 40% and other components' maxima summing only 57% → sum under 100% → deemed unclear. When claiming an alloy, list components and recite composition ranges exactly. See Part IX Chapter 7 for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must recite matters necessary to specify the invention (Article 42(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims shall recite such matters regarded necessary to specify what is sought for patent protection as structures, methods, functions and materials or combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an invention can be clearly specified by its effect or operation method rather than physical structure, the applicant may set forth the invention accordingly. Note: this provision does not by itself provide a ground for rejection or invalidation; an examiner shall not notify a ground for rejection based solely on this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and legal prescription of claim drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are prescribed in the law to ensure they determine the scope of protection; Korean law adopts a multiple-claims system allowing one or more claims directed to subject matters for which protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 5 of the Enforcement Decree prescribes claim drafting requirements under the multiple-claims system; claims should be drafted with the legal role of defining scope in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and discrimination of independent vs dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims narrow or add further limitations to specify an independent claim by adding technical elements or narrowing a generic concept to a species. Dependent claims are claims whose inventions are dependent on other claims and change accordingly when the referred claims change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim that narrows or adds limitations but does not refer formally to the other claim(s) is not a dependent claim. Conversely, a claim that formally refers to an independent claim but does not narrow or add limitations (e.g., substituting A with B without narrowing) is not a dependent claim. Article 5(1) allows claims that substantiate the independent claim by narrowing or adding to be presented as dependent, but they may also be presented as independent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent claims presentation (Article 5(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent claims shall be presented without referring to other claims in the form of standing alone; however, independent claims can refer to other claims within the scope in which the invention can be clearly understood to avoid redundant description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted examples include 'A product of … manufactured by the method of claim 1', 'A method of manufacturing a product of claim 1 by …', 'A method of … by using a product manufactured by the method of claim 1', 'A product manufactured with the device of claim 1'. Dependent claims must include the limitations of the claims they refer to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims that must be treated as independent despite referring
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be treated as independent (not dependent) where they are presented in the form of decreasing the elements of the claims referred to or substituting the subject matter set forth in the claims referred to with other matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1 recites a power transfer unit with a gear electric motor; Claim 2 recites the power transfer unit of claim 1 equipped with a belt conveyor instead of a gear electric motor — Claim 2 is treated as independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper number of claims (Article 5(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim shall be presented in a proper number according to the nature of the invention. Improper numbers include where two or more inventions of different categories are recited in one claim, where two or more subject matters are included, redundant identical claims, or where multiple claims are technically referred to many times within a single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: claiming two subject matters in one claim (e.g., a polymer and a contact lens using it) is improper. Referring to multiple claims repeatedly within a single claim (creating confusing nested references) is improper and may be exempted if it causes confusion similar to dependent claims referring to more than two claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include claim numbers when referring (Article 5(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim referring to other claims shall contain the number of the claims referred to and the numbers shall be entered in an appropriate manner (e.g., 'in claim 1', 'in any from claim 1 to claim 3').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 24645, effective July 1, 2013) applies to all claims making reference to other claims for applications examined after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate numbering for multiple-claim references (Article 5(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: As for a claim referring to two or more claims, the claims referred to shall be numbered alternatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between alternative listings ('in claim 1 or claim 2', 'in any of claims 1 to 3', etc.) which limit the claim to alternatives, and non-alternative listings ('in claim 1, claim 2') which are treated differently. Examples given illustrate alternative vs non-alternative listings, and how conjunctions 'and'/'or' and ranges are interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on nested multiple references (Article 5(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims referring to two or more claims cannot refer to other claims that themselves refer to two or more claims; this aims to prevent difficulties in interpreting chained references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show chains where Claim 4 refers to claim 2 or 3 and claim 3 already refers to claim 1 or 2 — such claims violate the provision. Violation leads to a ground for rejection citing Article 42(8) of the Patent Act. Note: the provision does not apply to claims depending from only one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence in claim numbering (Article 5(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim referred to by another claim should precede the other claim in numbering to facilitate interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim refers to itself or to a later-numbered claim, an examiner shall notify a ground for rejection citing violation of Article 42(8) and Article 5(7), or a ground for rejection citing indefiniteness under Article 42(4)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim presentation format: new line and sequential numbering (Article 5(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim shall be presented in a new line and the claims shall be numbered in sequence. To clearly define configuration even within a single claim, a claim can be presented in several lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a method claim can be structured with (A), (B), (C), (D) steps each on its own line to clarify procedural steps (e.g., heating, forging, re-heating, quenching).

rubrics_metrics.name: System for deferral of submission of claims (filing spec without claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may attach a specification without claims at filing (deferral system) to allow speedy filing and time to prepare claims, but claims must be submitted within a time limit (three months after notification of intention of request for examination or 1 year and 2 months from priority date; transitional periods for pre-2014 filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit claims by the deadline results in the application being deemed withdrawn the day after the deadline. If an applicant files a request for examination before submitting claims, the examiner shall return the written request and give opportunity for explanation. Applications filed without claims are not laid open for publication since they're deemed withdrawn once the deadline expires. Divisional/converted applications may have special extensions (claims may be submitted until 30 days from divisional/converted filing in certain cases). Whether deferral is used is determined by whether the 'Patent Claims' identification symbols are deleted in the specification form; presence of the heading means deferral is not employed (even if claims area contains blanks or punctuation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention: statutory requirements (Article 45 & Enforcement Decree Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single patent application may cover a group of inventions linked so as to form a single general inventive concept. Requirements: (1) the claimed inventions shall be technologically correlated; (2) the claimed inventions shall have the same or corresponding technological features, where such technological features are improvements over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'special technical features' refer to improvements compared with prior art; they need not be identical (e.g., providing elasticity via a spring vs a rubber block can be corresponding). Determination of unity generally requires consideration of prior art; unity may be determined a priori in some cases but often a posteriori after prior art search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and balancing considerations for unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 45 aims to balance convenience for applicants (ability to file related inventions together) with fairness to third parties and administrative efficiency for the Office; whether inventions form a single general inventive concept depends on whether claims share same or corresponding technological features (improvements over prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation should balance applicants' interest in filing multiple inventions in one application and third parties' interest in limiting inventions per application to avoid disadvantage in rights observation and prior art use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to determine unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity is determined by selecting a first invention, specifying its special technical features as improvements over prior art, selecting a second invention and its special technical features, then checking whether these special features are the same or corresponding; if so, the inventions form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) choose first invention and identify special technical features vs prior art (may include multiple features); (2) choose second invention and identify its special features; (3) check technical correlation by comparing special features; (4) iterate for all claims; (5) select first invention as subject to examination (and include inventions in the first technical group). Examiner must notify lack of unity on all claims and specify that concerned inventions do not share the same or corresponding special technical features. Lack of unity is a ground for rejection, not invalidation; examiners need not require divisional filings if examination can be completed without additional prior art search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and rules illustrating unity (generic/species, corresponding features, non-corresponding features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity is met when dependent claims include all special technical features of the independent claim (generic/species), when claims disclose corresponding special technical features (e.g., expander vs compressor as corresponding sub-combinations), and where combinations/sub-combinations exist. Unity is not met where claims recite distinct, non-corresponding special technical features (e.g., control circuit A vs control circuit B as separate special features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: (a) independent claim A+B with dependent claims adding C or D → unity; (b) claim 1 filament A, claim 2 lamp B comprising filament A, claim 3 searchlight comprising B → unity; (c) claims with corresponding sub-combinations (expander/compressor) → unity among claims; (d) claims with distinct special features → unity only where common features exist (e.g., claim1 with A and claim3 using A → unity; claim1 vs claim2 with different control circuits → not unity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity determination for product vs manufacturing method
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity between a product invention and a manufacturing method invention of that product is determined based on whether the manufacturing method is 'suitable' for manufacture of the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Suitable' means that when the manufacturing method is practiced, the product is manufactured. 'Suitable' does not mean the product cannot be manufactured by other methods or that the method cannot be used for other products. Examples: (1) chemical material X (product) and method for manufacturing X → common special technical feature is chemical material X → unity. (2) corrugated cardboard with cavity filled by intumescent resin and method of charging and heating → the product created by the method is the claimed product → unity.
